City Council
AGENDA
A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
June 3, 2013
07:00 P.M.
City Hall Council Chambers
24300 Narbonne Avenue
1.
OPENING CEREMONIES
a.
Call Meeting to Order
b.
Flag Salute
c.
Invocation - Councilmember Sanchez
d.
Roll Call
2.
APPROVAL OF AGENDA
3.
SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
Presentation of Certificates of Appointment to Kevin Jankowski (Public Safety and Traffic Commission), David Popelka (Planning Commission), and Steven Cammarata (Planning Commission).
Presentation of Certificates of Recognition to poster and slogan contest winners and sponsors for the "Follow me, I'm gang and drug free" walk.
4.
CITY MANAGER'S REPORT
5.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council Comments; however, items which are not will be limited to Council reports, announcements, or requests for clarification, or factual information, or to placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.
6.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
7.
CONSENT AGENDA
All items under the Consent Agenda are considered by the Council to be routine and will be enacted by one motion in the form listed below. There may be separate discussions of these items prior to the time the Council votes on the motion. Specific items may be removed from the Consent Agenda at the request of any Councilmember or staff.
a.
Motion to Waive Further Reading
b.
Recommendation to approve the minutes for a Special and Regular City Council meeting held on May 20, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Minutes- May 20, 2013
c.
Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 7.C
d.
Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 7.D
e.
Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 7.E
f.
Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 7.F
g.
Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 7.G
h.
Monthly Report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 7.H
i.
April 2013 Treasurer's Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.
Staff Report- item 7.I
j.
Approval of an Ordinance amending Sections 11-1.67.04(3)(C)(III) and 11-1.67.05(B) of the Lomita Municipal Code to add restrictions for the use of Light-Emitting Diodes (LEDS) in Signage and other matters properly related thereto. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 7.J
k.
Consider authorizing the Mayor sign a letter of support for Assembly Bill 488 (known as the "Primary Battery Recycling Act").
Staff Report- item 7.K
l.
Consider authorizing the Mayor to sign a letter opposing AB 1147 (Proposed Amendments to the State Massage Establishment regulations) unless amended.
Staff Report- item 7.L
m.
Final Acceptance of the Crenshaw Blvd./Lomita Blvd. Intersection Improvement Project by FS Construction (Phase 1). RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 7.M
n.
Final Acceptance of the Citywide Sidewalk and Pedestrian Safety Improvement Project by FS Construction. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.
Staff Report- item 7.N
PUBLIC HEARINGS
8.
ADOPTION OF 2013/14 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET Discussion and possible approval of the proposed budget for Fiscal Year 2013/14 and possible adoption of Resolutions:
No. 2013-30 Adopting the budget for FY 2013/14
No. 2013-31 Adopting the annual investment policy statement
No. 2013-32 Adopting the annual employee compensation plan and;
No. 2013-33 Confirming the factors used for calculating the GANN manual appropriations limit.
Presented by City Manager Rock and Administrative Services Director Chavez.
Staff Report- item 8
Staff Report- item 8-Final Draft Budget
9.
LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE DISTRICT NO.1 Discussion and possible approval of the assessment for the annual maintenance, operation, and servicing of the parkway landscaping along the north side of Palos Verdes Drive North (Landscape Maintenance District No.1), and Resolution No. 2013-27 approving the engineer's report and Resolution No. 2013-28 confirming the assessment for 2013/14.
Presented by Public Works Director Damasse.
Staff Report- item 9
10.
ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2013-06/INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE (PLANNING COMMISSION APPEAL PROCEDURES) Discussion and consideration of an Ordinance adding Section 11-1.70.16 (A) 1 to the Lomita Municipal Code establishing a procedure for a majority of the City Council to appeal a Planning Commission decision. On May 13, 2013, the Planning Commission considered recommending extending the appeal period for Planning Commission decisions from 15 calendar days to 21 calendar days. The Planning Commission recommended that the appeal period remain at the current 15 calendar days.
Presented by Assistant City Manager Sugano.
Staff Report- item 10
SCHEDULED MATTERS
11.
EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION PROGRAM Discussion and possible approval of the City of Lomita Employee Recognition Program.
Presented by Administrative Services Department Director Chavez
Staff Report- item 11
ADJOURNMENT
Written materials distributed to the City Council within 72 hours of the City Council meeting are available for public inspection immediately upon distribution in the City Clerk's office at 24300 Narbonne Avenue.
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) if you need special assistance to participate in this meeting, you should contact the office of the City Clerk at 310 325-7110 (voice) or the California Relay Service. Notification 48 hours prior to the meeting will enable the city to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility to this meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
June 3, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:03 p.m., on Monday, June
3, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Traina led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Public Works Director Damasse,
Community Services Director McPherron, Administrative Services Director Chavez, Parks and
Recreation Director Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

City Attorney Hogin made an announcement of the closed session after Item #2 on that agenda,
and stated that the City Council convened a Special Meeting at 6 p.m., and went into closed
session at 6 p.m. According to City Attorney Hogin, Council discussed both items listed on the
closed session agenda, with City Manager Rock being present during his evaluation, but
excused him during the second item, labor negotiations. No reportable action was taken on the
items listed on the closed session agenda.

3. SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Estrada and Councilmembers presented Certificates of Appointment to David Popelka
(Planning Commission) and Steven Cammarata (Planning Commission). Kevin Jankowski, who
had been appointed to the Public Safety and Traffic Commission, was absent.

Irene Kurata, Public Safety and Traffic Commissioner, presented Certificates of Recognition, and
awards for poster and slogan contest winners, to the participants in the "Follow me, I’m gang
and drug free" walk.

  Page 1
 4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock reported that the mobile command center will be delivered on June 14,
2013, and will be ready for use in July 2013, after it is fully equipped.

5. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina recommended that staff review the City of Torrance award agreement for
two pilot water wells (Memorandum of Agreement, dated April 23, 2013), which outlines
information about well water quality in Torrance. According to Councilmember Traina, he has
received several complaints from residents regarding chlorine in water, and he was concerned
to see in the water report that chlorine is in the quantity of three parts per million, while WMD
water is only two parts per million. Councilmember Traina asked staff to investigate why the
level of chlorine in blended Lomita water is higher than that of Metropolitan Water.

Councilmember Sanchez reported that Councilmembers Savidan, Gazeley, and Mayor Estrada,
along with himself, attended the Memorial Day event. Councilmember Sanchez also stated that
he attended the Community Day event at the Lomita Railroad Museum on June 1, 2013, and
thanked staff and volunteers for their hard work.

Councilmember Savidan stated that the Cypress Water Production Facility (CWPF) continues to
provide quality water to residents, and that he has personally been to the CWPF several times
to see operations and testing. According to Councilmember Savidan, the City provides high
quality water to residents, and he has never received any complaints from residents regarding
water quality. Councilmember Savidan also stated that he attended the "Follow me, I’m gang
and drug free" walk, which was sponsored by the Lomita Public Safety and Traffic Commission;
Councilmember Savidan noted that the event was very well put together.

Mayor Estrada reported that she also attended the "Follow me, I’m gang and drug free" walk,
and stated that it was a well-attended event.

Councilmember Gazeley stated that he attended the Memorial Day event, and wanted everyone
to be aware of the sacrifices that military men and women do daily for the country.

Councilmember Traina requested a copy of the daily pumping log from the CWPF.
Councilmember Traina stated that he noticed from the water report submitted to the Council that
polyphosphates are used in the water treatment process at CWPF, and added that he was not
made aware that the City was using polyphosphates until he received the report.
Councilmember Sanchez stated that the use of polyphosphates/chemicals was discussed at
previous Council meetings, and now is being used for water treatment.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Shienne VanEnk, President of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, thanked City Council for their
participation in, and support of, Chamber events. Ms. VanEnk also invited those in attendance
to the Chamber’s next Business Networking Mixer, which will take place at the Summer Studio’s
Academy on June 27, 2013, from 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m.

Bill Boyer, Lomita resident, wanted to know what the cost was for street sweeping, and also

  Page 2
 inquired as to the rationale behind the street sweeper cleaning the same street twice a week,
one day it is one side of the street and the other day it is the other side the street. Mr. Boyer
recommended that residents first be asked whether they would like their streets swept, and
possibly use the savings from street sweeping for street repairs.

Rob Friedrich, Lomita resident, stated that he had complained about the smell of sulfur in the
water last week. Mr. Friedrich went on to say that he wanted quality water.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, asked whether the City is licensed or sanctioned by the State of
California to use polyphosphates in the water. Mr. Albert provided information about how the
polyphosphate process works in water treatment. Mr. Albert stated that he would submit a
public records request for daily pumping logs from the CWPF.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Savidan
seconded the motion. Councilmember Traina requested to pull Item 7.C for discussion, and
Councilmember Sanchez requested to pull Item 7.E for discussion. The motion to approve the
Consent Agenda, minus Items 7.C and 7.E, was approved unanimously.

Item 7.C. - Councilmember Traina inquired about Invoice #5110529 for Water Works, and
specifically asked whether the purchase of chemicals was included in that amount. Public
Works Director Damasse responded that the payment to Water Works was for labor and
material for a period of time, including the purchase of chemicals. Public Works Director
Damasse also noted that staff is currently setting up a vendor account so that the City can start
ordering chemicals itself.

Item 7. E. - Councilmember Sanchez referred to the Planning Commission items in the
Community Development Department’s monthly report, and outlined the timeline of when City
Council received the information regarding Planning Commission decisions, as it relates directly
to the appeal process that will be discussed later in the Council meeting. Councilmember
Sanchez went on to note that it took almost 21 days for the Council to receive information
regarding decisions after action was taken by the Planning Commission.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve Items 7.C. and 7.E.  Councilmember Traina
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for a Special and Regular City Council Meeting
  held on May 20, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  Page 3
   g. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Monthly Report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. April 2013 Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  j. Approval of an Ordinance amending Sections 11-1.67.04(3)(C)(III) and 11-1.67.05(B) of
  the Lomita Municipal Code to add restrictions for the use of Light-Emitting Diodes (LEDS)
  in Signage and other matters properly related thereto. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  k. Consider authorizing the Mayor to sign a letter of support for Assembly Bill 488 (known as
  the “Primary Battery Recycling Act”).

  l. Consider authorizing the Mayor to sign a letter opposing AB 1147 (Proposed Amendments
  to the State Massage Establishment Regulations) unless amended.

  m. Final Acceptance of the Crenshaw Blvd./Lomita Blvd. Intersection Improvement Project by
  FS Construction (Phase 1). RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  n. Final Acceptance of the Citywide Sidewalk and Pedestrian Safety Improvement Project by
  FS Construction. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS:

8. ADOPTION OF 2013/14 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET

City Manager Rock stated that each individual City department presented their budget request
at the Budget Workshop held on May 22, 2013. City Manager Rock then provided a PowerPoint
presentation related to budget revenues, total expenditures, and a breakdown of General Fund
expenditures by department (Attachment A). According to City Manager Rock, General Fund
expenditures are mostly personnel-related costs (46%) and contract services (Sheriff’s
Departments contract 42%), with operations and maintenance being only 10% of the total
General Fund budget.

Administrative Services Director Chavez stated that total General Fund Reserve balance is
currently $3.8 million, and that changes suggested at the Budget Workshop had been
incorporated in the final draft of the FY 2013/14 budget, including the increase in travel and
training for Councilmembers, the elimination of the community contributions line item, and an
adjustment made to the mobile command center line item.

Councilmember Traina stated that at the Budget Workshop he requested a detailed breakdown
of the overhead costs for the Water Fund, which were in the amount of $110,000, in order to
better see how that number was calculated; Councilmember Traina stated that he had not
received any information regarding that request. According to Councilmember Traina, the
justification for that amount of funding needs to be provided, and in turn be available for the
public, as the rate payers have the right to know for what they are paying. City Manager Rock
responded that in 2012, as the result of the Salary Allocation Study, $171,000 was charged back
to the General Fund and that overhead costs were eliminated from the FY 2012/13 budget. City
Manager Rock further stated that staff would provide the detailed information regarding the
overhead costs to the Council. Councilmember Traina stated that he also requested justification

  Page 4
 for the Sheriff’s Department patrol of the CWPF, of which $25,000 was allocated to the Water
Fund.

Councilmember Traina stated that he calculated the City’s overtime costs, and overtime totals
$104,822. According to Councilmember Traina, overtime has been reduced over the years, but
the City should have a stricter policy governing the use of overtime. Councilmember Traina also
mentioned that he thought the allocation of labor to the Water Fund seemed high and should be
looked at again.

Mayor Estrada stated that on Page 23, Line Item 5755, and on Page 24, that those salaries had
been tabled and will be voted on at another time.

Mayor Estrada opened the public hearing.

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, stated that he had concerns about the allocation of employee
salaries in the Water Fund. Mr. McGrath also asked staff to look into the Sheriff’s Department’s
budget, as it includes GEM cars that have not been seen in Lomita. Lastly, Mr. McGrath asked
that City Council address the issue of employees’ salaries, as they are becoming much higher
than those of the private sector.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, inquired about the savings from the water blending, which
according to his calculations, and as indicated in the budget, are $250,000 a year, which means
that the total savings is only $4.46 per month, per rate payer.

Mayor Estrada closed the public hearing.

Councilmember Savidan moved to amend the budget by adding $2,000 to the Community
Contributions Line Item, with $1,000 being earmarked for the Lomita Little League and $1,000 to
the Sister City organization. Councilmember Savidan added that he researched this issue after
the Budget Workshop and found no violation in giving money to these community organizations.
Councilmember Savidan also recommended taking $2,000 from his travel and training budget in
order to cover the cost of the $2,000 he proposed. Discussion followed regarding the proposed
budget amendment, and most Councilmembers agreed that the $2,000 would come out of the
overall travel and training budget for the City Council. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the
motion.

Councilmember Traina recommended that Councilmembers make personal donations instead of
using the public’s money in contributing to community organizations. Discussion followed on
whether such community contributions were considered as gifts of public funds.

ROLL CALL:

AYES: Councilmembers Gazeley, Savidan, Sanchez, and Mayor Estrada
NOES: Councilmember Traina

Councilmember Gazeley moved to adopt the budget, including all four resolutions, but minus the
two expenses identified earlier. Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion.

ROLL CALL:

  Page 5
 AYES: Councilmembers Gazeley, Savidan, Sanchez, and Mayor Estrada
NOES: Councilmember Traina

9.  LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE DISTRICT NO.1

Public Works Director Damasse stated that the current Landscape Maintenance District
assessment has remained unchanged for years, and he recommended approval of the
Engineer’s Report and to leave the Landscape Maintenance District assessment the same.

Mayor Estrada opened the public hearing.

Dave Albert, Lomita resident, stated that this Landscape Maintenance District is maintained by a
contracted-out company, which works well, and in turn Mr. Albert recommended that the City
create other special districts in order to fix streets by contracting out with private companies to
perform the work cheaper. City Manager Rock stated that it would require a two-thirds vote of
the residents of Lomita for the creation of any new district.

Mayor Estrada closed the public hearing.

Councilmember Savidan moved to approve Item #9.  Councilmember Traina seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

10. ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT NO. 2013-06 - INTRODUCTION OF AN ORDINANCE
  (PLANNING COMMISSION APPEAL PROCEDURES)

Assistant City Manager Sugano stated that this item had been previously discussed on April 15,
2013, at which time City Council directed staff to prepare an ordinance to allow a majority of the
Council to appeal a decision of the Planning Commission and to extend the appeal process for
Planning Commission decisions to 21 calendar days. According to Assistant City Manager
Sugano, the Planning Commission recommended approval of the changes, except to leave the
timeframe for appeal at 15 calendar days.

Councilmember Sanchez expressed his concern that City Council would not have enough time
to appeal Planning Commission decisions even with the proposed 21 calendar days, and in turn
Councilmember Sanchez recommended extending the appeal time to 28 calendar days, so that
Council has sufficient time to review, and if necessary act on, Planning Commission decisions.
Instead of 28 calendar days, Assistant City Manager Sugano recommended 30 calendar days
for the appeal process, which would allow for a time frame of two City Council meetings to
appeal Planning Commission decisions.

Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve the first reading of the proposed ordinance, and to
extend the appeal process to 30 calendar days, instead of 15 calendar days. Councilmember
Gazeley seconded the motion. City Attorney Hogin restated the motion for the record, which
carried unanimously.

SCHEDULED MATTERS

11. EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION PROGRAM
  Discussion and possible approval of the City of Lomita Employee Recognition Program.

  Page 6
 Administrative Services Director Chavez provided an overview of the staff report, and stated that
the financial impact of the proposed Employee Recognition Program is estimated to be less than
$1,000.

Councilmember Savidan recommended that staff look into the legality of giving a day off to the
Employee of the Year, as it could be considered a gift of public funds. Mayor Estrada moved to
receive and file the staff report. Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried
unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8:30 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC

  Page 7
